saira: heads-up — ran a long-context soak on nova-encoder-30b-int4 (16k+ context) and hit a weird token divergence that looks like kvcache race / corruption. repro ~2/30 runs. anyone around to eyeball logs? :thinking:

ben: can you paste the minimal repro and the exact command you ran? was this on dedicated or local bench?

saira: dedicated pool d-gpu-b4, config: --max-seq 18000 --batch 4 --streaming off. command: `python -m tests.longctx_kv --model nova-encoder-30b-int4 --steps 18000 --seed 42 --batch 4`

saira: pasted an excerpt of the stderr from the failing run:
```
[2026-02-12 09:12:15] kvcache: append shard=2 pos=16382 len=4
[2026-02-12 09:12:15] kvcache: writeback started token=16384
[2026-02-12 09:12:15] attention: rope-scale=linear on
[2026-02-12 09:12:15] model: quant=int4
[2026-02-12 09:12:15] ERROR: kv-checksum mismatch at global_pos=16384 expected=0x7f got=0x1a
[2026-02-12 09:12:15] trace: shard=2 thread=worker-7 last_write_ts=167..
```

oliver: interesting. error looks like a stale write overlapping with a prefetch. did you try running with REDWOOD_KV_LOCK=1 or setting `KV_WRITE_PARALLELISM=1`?

saira: not yet. just re-ran with REDWOOD_KV_LOCK=1 and got 0/6 failures so far (previously 2/6). will run overnight.

jamal: if lock reduces it, could be concurrency ordering issue between prefill and streaming writes. can you also try `--no-prefill` and `--prefill-only` modes to isolate?

saira: good call. quick matrix I'm going to run tonight:
- int4 vs int8
- rope linear scaling on/off (`--rope-scale linear|none`)
- prefill vs streaming
- KV_WRITE_PARALLELISM=1 vs 4

ben: also capture a kv-dump at failure. small helper: `REDWOOD_DUMP_KV_ON_ERROR=1 python -m tests.longctx_kv ...` will write /tmp/kv-dump-<ts>.bin. if you can share one of those we'll diff with a known-good run.

saira: pinned a dump: /tmp/kv-dump-1808881234-1.bin (uploaded to the thread). note: dump shows two entries overlapping around offset 0x3f00..0x4100.

eva: curious whether quantized packing changes alignment so a partial write overwrote neighbor. jamal, oliver — any suggestions for a quick parity-check tool?

jamal: I have a tiny script that validates per-token kv checksums and RoPE phase continuity. `tools/kv_inspect.py --dump /tmp/kv-dump-... --check-rope` — it'll flag sudden discontinuities in the rotary phase vector which look like wrong offset writes.

oliver: also try running with `ROPE_SHIFT_DEBUG=1` env to log pos->phase mapping. if the phase jumps then we know it's a write-shift not a model attention bug.

saira: running the matrix now. first observation: int8 + KV_WRITE_PARALLELISM=4 had 0/20 failures, int4 + parallelism=4 had 3/20. switching to single-threaded write drops int4 failures to 0/20.

ben: that strongly suggests a race in int4 write path. int4 packing probably writes smaller granularity so interleaves more. can you file a minimal reproducer that toggles just pack/parallelism?

saira: yes — i'll trim to a 2k-step repro that reproduces quickly. putting together steps and a small patch to dump pre/post kv contents.

ci-bot: build 1245 for branch feature/kv-lock-probe completed — unit tests passed :white_check_mark:

jamal: if you can reproduce quickly we can run ASAN-enabled build to catch invalid memory shuffles. even if quantized kernels are in JIT, ASAN on CPU path sometimes surfaces order bugs.

saira: noted. one more oddity — toggling `--rope-scale none` reduced repro rate even with int4+parallelism=4 (from 3/20 to 1/20). so RoPE scaling interacts somehow. maybe rotation offsets get applied before/after packing?

oliver: plausible — RoPE code path touches the kv buffers for phase factors; if int4 pack reorders bytes, concurrent mul-adds could see mixed phase factors. worth heavy instrumentation.

eva: for quality/eval side — do we have a golden eval (LLMQA) on long context to check whether these corruption cases actually change downstream outputs or are mostly token-level noise?

saira: good point. i'll snapshot model outputs from failing run and compare against a golden run (int8 single-threaded). initial diff shows token substitutions around the tail but coherent text until end. not catastrophic but unacceptable for RL scenarios.

ben: please open a ticket linking dumps + repro + matrix results. tag infra/runtime and eng-ml. i'd assign to oliver/jamal to triage next sprint.

saira: creating ticket now: INF-3892 — "intermittent KV write overlap with int4 packing under parallel writes affecting RoPE phase" — attaching dumps, logs, and short repro. pinging @oliver @jamal.

oliver: thanks. i'll start a bisect between quant kernels and the KV writer changes. jamal — can you add the rope-shift trace in the next run?

jamal: on it. also will try a microbench that repeatedly writes small kv records to stress alignment.

saira: thanks team. will update ticket with results tomorrow. :rocket:
